named_confounds: early-period sparsity (752 early vs 6014 late works)
one passage per work sampling noise
automated domain-label error that may vary by period
rationale: Data: 6766 works with one passage each; all have a year. Rate = count__domains__DISTANCE_TRAVEL / n_passages. Cutoff is 1876, with late defined as year >= 1876. Estimand: within each of 8 genres, take the unweighted mean of work rates for late works minus early works, then average the 8 genre differences equally. The result is +0.0517. The 95% CI is [0.031, 0.069], from a 2000-replicate bootstrap that resamples works within each genre x period cell. The late rate is higher than the early rate in all 8 genres, with differences of about +0.045 to +0.060. Two genres (domestic_realist, romance) have zero early occurrences. Robustness checks: high date-confidence only gives 0.049, low only 0.045, medium only 0.055, and excluding low gives 0.053. Single-edition works only give 0.051. By origin: UK 0.039, US 0.032, unknown 0.064. Decade means rise from about 0.03-0.07 before 1880 to about 0.11-0.12 after 1890. Caveats: the early period is thin (35-165 works per genre), so early estimates are noisy. Each work contributes one sampled passage. Labels come from a classifier, and if its errors differ by period they could mimic a trend. I did not cluster by author. Genre stratification controls for shifts in genre mix, but not for changes within a genre such as subgenre or publisher selection. The cited passage IDs are passages labelled with this domain, and they only illustrate it. The trend rests on the aggregate rates.
